quiz.q: Which kinds of transport use ATP? Put each one in the right group.
quiz.e: Diffusion, osmosis and facilitated diffusion happen on their own, from high to low. The Na-K pump moves substances from low to high, and phagocytosis and exocytosis form vesicles. These three use ATP.

quiz.q: A plant cell has an osmotic pressure of 12 atm and a turgor pressure of 5 atm. What is its suction force in atm?
quiz.e: Suction force is osmotic pressure minus turgor pressure: 12 − 5 = 7 atm. As the cell takes in water, turgor rises and suction force falls.

quiz.q: Put in order what happens to a plant cell placed in salt water.
ogeler: The outside becomes hypertonic to the cell
Water leaves the vacuole by osmosis
The vacuole shrinks and turgor pressure drops
The membrane pulls away from the wall (plasmolysis)
quiz.e: When the outside is more concentrated, water leaves the cell, the vacuole shrinks and turgor is lost. Finally the membrane pulls away from the wall. If the cell is put in pure water, the process reverses. This is called deplasmolysis.

quiz.q: Match each event with its kind of transport.
ciftler: A white blood cell engulfing a bacterium
A cell taking in a fluid droplet
quiz.e: Engulfing a solid particle is called phagocytosis, and taking in a fluid droplet is called pinocytosis. A vesicle fusing with the membrane and emptying its contents is called exocytosis. The diffusion of water across the membrane is osmosis.

mitoz.title: Mitosis and asexual reproduction
mitoz.summary: How does a cell split in two, and how do living things multiply from a single parent?

cards.h: The cell cycle: interphase and M
cards.p: The time from a cell's formation to its division is called the cell cycle. The longest stage is interphase. The cell grows in G1, copies its DNA in S and prepares to divide in G2. Then come mitosis and cytokinesis, the division of the cytoplasm.

etk.soru: Put the stages of the cell cycle in order, starting with G<sub>1</sub>.

cards.p: The loose DNA in interphase is called chromatin. During division, chromatin shortens and thickens and is then called a chromosome. A copied chromosome is made of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere. In humans, 2n = 46.

cards.p: Prophase is the first stage of mitosis. The chromosomes become visible, and the nuclear envelope and nucleolus disappear. In an animal cell, the centrosomes move to the poles and spindle fibers form between them.

cards.h: Metaphase: a single line at the equator
cards.p: In metaphase, spindle fibers attach to the centromeres, and the chromosomes line up in a single row at the equator. As you just found, the chromosomes are at their shortest and most distinct in this stage. That is why a karyotype is made in this stage.

once.soru: What is pulled to opposite poles in anaphase?

secenekler.neden: Once the centromere splits, each chromatid is pulled to its own pole.
The nuclear envelope already disappeared in prophase.
The centrosomes are already at the poles. What gets pulled to the poles are the chromatids.

cards.p: In telophase, the chromosomes loosen and the nuclear envelope forms again. Then the cytoplasm divides. This is called cytokinesis. An animal cell divides by pinching in at the middle. A plant cell builds a cell plate in the middle.

cards.h: DNA and chromosomes stage by stage
cards.p: In a cell with 2n = 4, the amount of DNA rises from 2 units to 4 units in the S phase. After cytokinesis, each daughter cell gets 2 units. The number of chromosomes is 8 only in anaphase and telophase.

once.soru: A human cell with 2n = 46 divided by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell?

secenekler.neden: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same. A 2n cell gives 2n cells again.
The division that halves the chromosome number is meiosis.
92 chromosomes are seen only for a short time, in anaphase.

cards.h: Why mitosis matters and how it is controlled
cards.p: Mitosis allows growth, repair and renewal. In single-celled eukaryotes, it is also a way to reproduce. The cycle has checkpoints at G1, G2 and metaphase. If this control breaks down, cancer can develop.

once.soru: Which kind of division closes a cut on your hand?

secenekler.neden: The skin cells at the edge of the wound divide by mitosis and fill the gap.
Meiosis only makes reproductive cells.
Cells cannot fill the gap just by growing. New cells are needed.

cards.p: In asexual reproduction, a single parent is enough and there is no fertilization. The offspring are genetically identical to the parent. Amoebas and euglenas divide by mitosis. A bacterium's binary fission is not mitosis, because a bacterium has no nucleus.

once.soru: An outgrowth forms on a yeast cell, grows and breaks off. What kind of reproduction is this?

secenekler.neden: A small bud grows on the parent. The offspring is smaller than the parent.
In fission, the parent splits in two and the two offspring are about equal.
A spore is a single cell, and many of them form inside sacs.

cards.p: Regrowing a lost part is called regeneration. If the broken-off piece becomes a whole individual, it counts as reproduction. Planarians reproduce this way. In parthenogenesis, an unfertilized egg develops. Male honeybees (n) form this way.

once.soru: A lizard regrows its lost tail. Is this reproduction?

secenekler.neden: No new individual forms. Only the lost part is regrown.
Reproduction requires a new individual. The tail does not become an individual.

secenekler.yazi: Yes, if the tail is long
secenekler.neden: The length of the tail does not matter, because no new individual forms.

cards.p: In tissue culture, a few plant cells grow into a whole plant in a sterile medium. In cloning, the nucleus of a body cell is moved into an egg whose nucleus has been removed. Dolly the sheep was born this way in 1996.

once.soru: Dolly's nuclear DNA is the same as which sheep's?

secenekler.neden: The nucleus moved into the egg carries all of Dolly's nuclear DNA.
The egg's nucleus had been removed.
The surrogate mother only grows the embryo.

cards.p:
• The cell cycle is made of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis and cytokinesis. DNA is copied in the S phase.
• Chromosomes appear in prophase, line up at the equator in metaphase, chromatids separate in anaphase and nuclei form in telophase.
• Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same.
• In asexual reproduction, the offspring are usually identical to the parent.

quiz.q: Put the events in an animal cell's cycle in order.
ogeler: Chromosomes appear and the nuclear envelope disappears
Chromosomes line up in a single row at the equator
Sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles
The nuclear envelope forms again at the poles
The cytoplasm pinches in and divides
quiz.e: DNA is copied in the S phase of interphase. Then chromosomes appear in prophase, line up at the equator in metaphase and their chromatids separate in anaphase. Nuclei form in telophase, and cytokinesis comes last.

quiz.q: A human cell with 2n = 46 chromosomes is going through mitosis. How many chromatids does this cell have in metaphase?
quiz.e: In the S phase, every chromosome is copied and carries two sister chromatids. That is why there are 46 × 2 = 92 chromatids.

quiz.q: Match each example with its type of asexual reproduction.
ciftler: A piece of planarian becoming an individual
quiz.e: An amoeba divides by mitosis, yeast buds and bread mold makes spores in a sporangium. A cut piece of planarian becomes a whole individual by regeneration. A male honeybee develops from an unfertilized egg. This is called parthenogenesis.

quiz.q: In a cell going through mitosis, which of these shows that it is a plant cell?
o: Spindle fibers forming
Chromosomes lining up at the equator
Sister chromatids separating
The cytoplasm dividing with a cell plate
quiz.e: Spindle fibers forming, chromosomes lining up at the equator and chromatids separating happen in both kinds of cell. A cell plate, however, forms only in plant cells.
y: Spindle fibers also form in animal cells. What is unique to plants is division with a cell plate.
Chromosomes line up at the equator in every mitosis. What is unique to plants is the cell plate.
Sister chromatids separate in the anaphase of every mitosis. What marks a plant is the cytoplasm dividing with a cell plate.

mayoz.title: Meiosis and sexual reproduction
mayoz.summary: How is the chromosome number halved, and where does variety come from?

cards.p: If gametes carried as many chromosomes as body cells, the chromosome number would double in every generation. Meiosis halves the chromosome number (2n → n). In animals it makes gametes, and in plants it makes spores.

cards.p: In a diploid cell, every chromosome has a partner. One comes from the mother and the other from the father. These partners are called homologous chromosomes. Homologs have the same length, shape and order of genes. Humans have 23 homologous pairs.

once.soru: Of the 46 chromosomes in a human body cell, how many come from the mother?

secenekler.neden: One of each pair comes from the mother and the other from the father.
Not all 46 chromosomes come from a single parent.
Half of them come from the mother.

cards.p: Before meiosis, DNA is copied once. In prophase I, homologous chromosomes line up side by side along their whole length. This is called synapsis. The structure of four chromatids is called a tetrad. Tetrads do not form in mitosis.

cards.p: In metaphase I, the tetrads line up at the equator in pairs. In anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles, and the centromeres do not split. At the end of telophase I, two n cells form, but the chromosomes still have two chromatids.

cards.p: DNA is not copied between meiosis I and meiosis II. Meiosis II is like mitosis, and in anaphase II the sister chromatids separate. The result is four haploid cells that are genetically different from one another.

once.soru: When a germ cell completes meiosis, how many cells form?

secenekler.neden: Two divisions come one after the other. One cell first becomes two, then four.
In meiosis, the cell divides twice. That is why four cells form, not two.
DNA is copied once, but the cell divides twice. The result is 4 cells.

cards.h: DNA and chromosome number in meiosis
cards.p: In a cell with 2n = 4, the amount of DNA rises from 2 units to 4 units in the S phase. It drops to 2 units in telophase I and to 1 unit in telophase II. The number of chromosomes drops from 4 to 2 in meiosis I.

once.soru: In which division of meiosis is the chromosome number halved?

secenekler.neden: When the homologs separate, each cell gets only one of each pair. This drops the number from 2n to n.
Meiosis II separates sister chromatids. By this stage, the chromosome number is already n.
The chromosome number is halved only once, in meiosis I.

cards.p: Both mitosis and meiosis start with DNA copying. Mitosis allows growth, repair and asexual reproduction, and it keeps the chromosome number the same. Meiosis makes gametes or spores, halves the chromosome number and creates variety.

cards.p: There are three sources of variety. The first is crossing over. The second is the independent assortment of homologs in metaphase I. This creates 2n kinds of gametes, and in humans that number is about 8.4 million. The third is the random joining of gametes at fertilization.

once.soru: How many eggs does one egg mother cell give through meiosis?

secenekler.neden: The cytoplasm does not divide equally. One cell becomes the egg, and the others become small polar bodies.
In males four sperm form, but in females only one egg forms.
The polar bodies do not become eggs. Only one egg forms.

cards.p: The joining of the sperm and egg nuclei is called fertilization. Two n gametes join and form a 2n zygote. In fish and frogs, external fertilization happens in water. In reptiles, birds and mammals, internal fertilization happens inside the female's body.

etk.soru: Sort each animal by how fertilization happens.
ogeler: A frog releases its eggs and sperm into water. Fertilization happens outside the body.
A dolphin lives in water, but it is a mammal. Fertilization happens inside the female's body.

once.soru: How many sets of chromosomes does the zygote formed by fertilization carry?

secenekler.neden: A sperm (n) and an egg (n) join. So n + n = 2n.
Gametes are the ones with n chromosomes. A zygote forms when two gametes join.
Each gamete brings one set of chromosomes. That makes two sets in total.

cards.p: In asexual reproduction, a single parent gives offspring like itself. This is fast, but there is little variety. Sexual reproduction involves meiosis and fertilization. The offspring differ both from their parents and from one another.

once.soru: If conditions suddenly change, which population has a better chance of survival?

secenekler.neden: The offspring differ from one another. That is why some of them can adapt to the new conditions.
The individuals are nearly all the same, so one change affects them all at once.
Variety is a big advantage in a changing environment.

cards.p:
• In meiosis, DNA is copied once, the cell divides twice and 4 different n cells form.
• Homologs separate in meiosis I, and sister chromatids separate in meiosis II.
• Variety comes from crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilization.
• Nondisjunction leads to outcomes such as Down syndrome.
• In plants, spores form by meiosis and gametes by mitosis.

quiz.q: Put the events of meiosis in order.
ogeler: Homologs pair up into tetrads and cross over
Tetrads line up in pairs at the equator
Homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles
Sister chromatids move to opposite poles
quiz.e: DNA is copied once before meiosis. In prophase I, tetrads form and crossing over happens. In metaphase I the tetrads line up in pairs, and in anaphase I the homologs separate. In anaphase II the sister chromatids separate, and four n cells form.

quiz.q: In an organism with 2n = 8, the homologs differ from each other and there is no crossing over. How many kinds of gametes can form by independent assortment?
quiz.e: The number of homologous pairs is n = 4. Independent assortment gives 2<sup>4</sup> = 16 kinds of gametes.

quiz.q: Sort each event by the division it happens in.
ogeler: Can happen in a haploid cell
quiz.e: Tetrads, crossing over and homologs separating are unique to meiosis. A haploid cell can only go through mitosis, and mitosis gives identical cells. DNA copying, centromeres splitting and spindle fibers are found in both divisions.

quiz.q: In a human (2n = 46), meiosis I goes normally. In meiosis II, the sister chromatids of one chromosome fail to separate in just one of the two cells. What are the chromosome numbers of the four gametes?
quiz.e: At the end of meiosis I, both cells have 23 chromosomes. The cell with nondisjunction gives gametes with 24 and 22 chromosomes, and the normal cell gives gametes with 23 and 23.
y: This pattern belongs to nondisjunction in meiosis I. In meiosis II, only one cell is affected.
The two gametes from the cell with nondisjunction cannot be normal. One gets an extra chromosome, and the other is missing one.
Gametes are haploid. 47 and 45 chromosomes can only appear after fertilization, in the zygote.

siniflandirma.title: Classifying living things
siniflandirma.summary: How are living things grouped, and how are species named?

cards.p: More than one and a half million species of living things have been named so far. Classification means grouping living things by shared traits. This makes it easier to identify them, see how they are related and share information.

once.soru: About how many species of living things have been named on Earth?

secenekler.neden: New species are found every year too. Memorizing so many species one by one is impossible. That is why we group living things.
There are more than 10,000 bird species alone.
The number of insect species alone is close to a million.

cards.p: Artificial classification looks at appearance. So it puts the bat and the eagle in a "flyers" group. Natural classification looks at relatedness and compares homologous organs, embryos and DNA. By this classification, the bat is a mammal.

once.soru: Both bats and eagles fly. But a bat gives birth to live young and feeds them milk. Which group does the bat belong to?

secenekler.neden: By natural classification, which looks at relatedness, the bat is a mammal. Its wing has the same origin as a human arm.
Flying is a shared job, but it does not show relatedness. Bats have no feathers and nurse their young.
A bat has a skeleton and is not closely related to insects.

cards.p: Living things are placed in nested levels. From broadest to narrowest, these levels are: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. The basic unit of classification is the species.

cards.h: What is a species? The mule example
cards.p: In sexually reproducing organisms, a species is made up of individuals that can mate with each other and produce fertile offspring. The fact that mules are sterile shows that horses and donkeys are separate species. In bacteria, species are told apart by their DNA.

cards.p: Linnaeus gave each species a two-word Latin name. First comes the genus name with a capital letter, then the species name in lowercase. The name is written in italics: Homo sapiens.

cards.p: Living things are first divided into three domains: Bacteria, Archaea and Eukaryotes. The first two are prokaryotes. But archaea are not bacteria and are more closely related to eukaryotes.

cards.key: There are six kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, Protists, Plants, Fungi and Animals.

once.soru: Bacteria and archaea are both single-celled organisms with no nucleus. Are they in the same group?

secenekler.neden: Their cell walls and some of their molecules differ. By DNA, archaea are closer to eukaryotes than bacteria are.
Having no nucleus is a shared trait, but archaea are not bacteria.
Archaea are cellular organisms, not viruses.

cards.p: Bacteria and archaea are both single-celled prokaryotes. Bacteria have peptidoglycan in their cell walls, and archaea do not. Bacteria break down wastes, fix nitrogen and can cause disease. Archaea often live in extremely hot or salty places.

cards.p: Eukaryotes that are not plants, fungi or animals are called protists. Plants have cellulose walls and carry out photosynthesis. Fungi have chitin walls. They digest food outside themselves and absorb it. Animals have no cell wall.

cards.p: Most protists are single-celled. The amoeba moves with false feet, and the paramecium moves with cilia. Euglena carries out photosynthesis in light and takes in ready-made food in the dark. Plasmodium causes malaria.
cards.key: Euglena can feed both as an autotroph and as a heterotroph.

once.soru: Euglena carries out photosynthesis in light and takes in ready-made food in the dark. Which kingdom is it in?

secenekler.neden: Euglena is a single-celled eukaryote. It does not belong to the plant or animal kingdom.
Euglena carries out photosynthesis, but it is single-celled and also takes in ready-made food. So it is not a plant.
Euglena takes in ready-made food, but it has chloroplasts. So it is not an animal.

cards.p: Most fungi are multicellular and made of threads called hyphae. Most break down dead remains. Yeast makes bread rise. A lichen is a fungus and an alga living together. The alga makes food, and the fungus protects the alga.

once.soru: Lichens that live on bare rock are actually a partnership of two organisms. Which two?

secenekler.neden: The alga makes food by photosynthesis. The fungus holds water and protects the alga.
A lichen is neither a plant nor an animal.
One partner can be a cyanobacterium, but the other is always a fungus.

cards.h: Why aren't viruses in any kingdom?
cards.p: As you saw in the first topic, viruses are not cells. Kingdoms were set up for cellular organisms. So viruses are not placed in any kingdom and are studied separately.

once.soru: Why aren't viruses placed in any kingdom?

secenekler.neden: Kingdoms were set up for cellular organisms. A virus is not a cell, so it is studied separately.
Bacteria are small too, but they belong to a kingdom. The test is being a cell, not size.
Being harmful is not a classification criterion.

cards.p:
• Science uses natural classification, based on relatedness.
• Moving down toward species, the number of species decreases, and shared traits and relatedness increase.
• Individuals that can produce fertile offspring belong to the same species. The mule is sterile.
• The binomial name is written in italics, and the genus starts with a capital letter.
• There are three domains and six kingdoms. Viruses are not in any kingdom.

quiz.q: Find where humans fit in classification. Match each level with the human group at that level.
quiz.e: Humans are in the animal kingdom, the chordate phylum, the mammal class, the primate order and the genus Homo. The species name is Homo sapiens.

quiz.q: Put each organism in its kingdom.
quiz.e: A cyanobacterium is a bacterium that carries out photosynthesis. The amoeba, euglena, paramecium and plasmodium are single-celled eukaryotic protists. Yeast, mold and mushrooms are in the fungus kingdom.

quiz.q: Match each term with its correct description.
ciftler: Those that can produce fertile offspring
First word of a binomial name
quiz.e: Individuals that can produce fertile offspring form a species, and the first word of a binomial name is the genus. Natural classification looks at relatedness, and artificial classification at appearance. The broadest level is the domain.

quiz.q: Which is an example of homologous organs?
o: A bird wing and a fly wing
A human arm and a whale flipper
A bat wing and a butterfly wing
A rose thorn and a hedgehog spine
quiz.e: A human arm and a whale flipper come from the same bone layout. Their origin is the same, but their jobs differ. Natural classification looks at similarities like this.
y: Both are for flying, but their origins differ. These are analogous organs.
Their jobs are the same, but their origins differ. This is a pair of analogous organs.
The plant's thorn and the animal's spine are only similar in job. Their origins are completely different.

hayvanlar-alemi.title: The animal kingdom: invertebrates and vertebrates
hayvanlar-alemi.summary: How do you tell the invertebrate phyla and vertebrate classes apart?

once.soru: An organism is multicellular, has no cell wall and takes in food by swallowing it. Which kingdom is it in?

secenekler.neden: Animals are multicellular, have no cell wall and are heterotrophs. They take in food by swallowing it.
Plants have a cellulose wall, and they carry out photosynthesis.
Fungi have a chitin wall. They digest food outside the body and absorb it.

cards.p: Vertebrates have a backbone made of vertebrae along their back, and it protects the spinal cord. Invertebrates have no backbone, but some of them have an exoskeleton. About 95% of animal species are invertebrates.

ogeler: It has an internal skeleton of chalky plates under its skin, but no backbone.
It has well-developed eyes and a nervous system, but it is a mollusk and has no backbone.
Its skeleton is made of cartilage, but it has a backbone. It is a cartilaginous fish.
It looks like a fish, but it is a mammal and a vertebrate.

once.soru: A sponge passes water through the holes in its body. How does it get its food?

secenekler.neden: A sponge filters the food carried by the water that enters its pores. An adult sponge lives attached to one spot.
A sponge has no tentacles and no mouth.
Animals do not carry out photosynthesis.

cards.p: Flatworms have a flattened body, and most are parasites. Roundworms have a separate mouth and anus. The body of segmented worms is made of rings. They have a closed circulatory system, which means the blood always stays inside vessels.

once.soru: A tapeworm lives in the human intestine and has no digestive system. How does it feed?

secenekler.neden: A tapeworm absorbs the digested food in the intestine through its body surface. It is a parasitic flatworm.
A tapeworm does not suck blood. It absorbs the ready food in the intestine.
Animals do not carry out photosynthesis.

cards.p: Mollusks have a soft body. Most of them have a chalky shell made by the mantle. A snail's shell is one piece, while a mussel's shell has two parts. An octopus has no outer shell, and it is a very intelligent animal.

once.soru: Which one has no outer shell but is still a mollusk?

secenekler.neden: An octopus has no outer shell. It is an intelligent mollusk with well-developed eyes and a nervous system.
A snail has a one-piece shell.
A mussel has a two-part shell.

cards.p: The largest phylum is the arthropods. Their body is covered by an exoskeleton made of chitin, and they molt in order to grow. An insect has 3 pairs of legs, and a spider has 4 pairs. That is why a spider is not an insect.

once.soru: A starfish has an internal skeleton of chalky plates under its skin. Is a starfish a vertebrate?

secenekler.neden: A starfish has an internal skeleton, but no backbone. That is why it is an invertebrate.
Having an internal skeleton does not mean having a backbone.
A starfish larva has no backbone either.

cards.p: Fish breathe with gills and swim with fins. Their heart has two chambers, and their body temperature changes with the surroundings. A shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, while an anchovy's skeleton is made of bone.

once.soru: How does a fish breathe in water?

secenekler.neden: Gills take up the oxygen dissolved in the water.
Most fish have no lungs. Fish breathe with gills.
Breathing through the skin matters for frogs. A fish breathes with gills.

cards.p: Amphibians such as frogs and salamanders lay eggs without shells in water. Their larvae are called tadpoles, and a tadpole breathes with gills. The tadpole goes through metamorphosis and turns into an adult with lungs. An amphibian's heart has three chambers.

once.soru: A tadpole, the young of a frog, breathes with gills in water. What does an adult frog breathe with?

secenekler.neden: The lungs develop during metamorphosis. An adult frog also breathes through its moist skin.
The gills disappear during metamorphosis.
An adult frog also has lungs. Breathing through the skin only helps them.

cards.p: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. This reduces water loss. Reptiles breathe with lungs and lay shelled eggs on land. Most have a three-chambered heart, but a crocodile's heart has four chambers. Their body temperature changes with the surroundings.

once.soru: A jellyfish has no brain, but when you touch it, its whole body reacts. What is its nervous system like?

secenekler.neden: In hydras and jellyfish, nerve cells spread through the body like a net. That is why a signal travels in every direction.
A brain and a spinal cord are found in vertebrates.
The animals with no nerve cells are sponges. A jellyfish has nerve cells.

cards.p:
• Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic. Their cells have no wall.
• About 95% of species are invertebrates. The largest phylum is the arthropods.
• The heart has 2 chambers in fish, 3 in amphibians and most reptiles, and 4 in birds and mammals.
• Body temperature is constant only in birds and mammals.

quiz.q: Match each animal with its phylum.
quiz.e: A jellyfish is a cnidarian with stinging cells, a tapeworm is a flatworm, and a leech is a segmented worm. An octopus is a mollusk without a shell, and a starfish is an echinoderm.

quiz.q: Sort each animal by its body temperature.
quiz.e: Body temperature is constant only in birds and mammals. A penguin is a bird. A bat, a dolphin and a platypus are mammals. In fish, amphibians and reptiles, body temperature varies.

quiz.q: Match each set of features with its vertebrate class.
ciftler: Moist skin and lungs, three chambers
quiz.e: Gills and a two-chambered heart belong to fish, and moist skin and a three-chambered heart belong to amphibians. Dry scaly skin and shelled eggs belong to reptiles. Feathers are found only in birds, and hair and mammary glands only in mammals.

quiz.q: Which feature shows for certain that an animal is a vertebrate?
o: A closed circulatory system
A backbone made of vertebrae along its back
A skeleton that supports its body
Breathing with lungs
quiz.e: Earthworms and octopuses also have closed circulation. Arthropods have a skeleton too, in the form of an exoskeleton. Fish breathe with gills, not lungs. The feature that defines a vertebrate is the backbone.
y: Invertebrates such as the earthworm also have closed circulation. What sets vertebrates apart is the backbone.
An insect's exoskeleton also supports its body. What shows for certain that an animal is a vertebrate is a backbone made of vertebrae.
Fish are vertebrates, but they breathe with gills. The sure test is having a backbone.

bitkiler-alemi.title: The plant kingdom and plant groups
bitkiler-alemi.summary: Plant groups from mosses to flowering plants, alternation of generations, and monocots and dicots

cards.h: What makes a plant a plant
cards.p: Plants are eukaryotic and multicellular. Their cell walls are made of cellulose. They make food by photosynthesis and store the extra as starch. They protect their embryos inside a tissue.

cards.key: Chlorophyll a and b and cellulose are also found in green algae. Protecting the embryo, however, is unique to land plants. That is why they are called embryophytes.

once.soru: In what form does a plant store the extra food it makes by photosynthesis?

secenekler.neden: Glucose molecules join to form starch. Potatoes and wheat are examples of this store.
Glycogen is the storage substance of animals and fungi.
Cellulose is not a storage substance. It is the building material of the cell wall.

cards.p: Plants living on land faced the problems of drying out, moving water and reproducing. The cuticle reduced water loss, stomata controlled gas exchange and vascular bundles carried water. Pollen and seeds freed reproduction from depending on water.

etk.soru: Put each plant in the right group.
ogeler: A fern has vascular bundles, but no seeds. It reproduces with spores.
A pine is a gymnosperm. Its seed sits exposed on a cone scale.

cards.p: Mosses and liverworts have no vascular bundles and no true roots, stems or leaves. They hold on with rhizoids and stay short. Their sperm reach the egg by swimming through water, so they live in damp places.

once.soru: Why do mosses mostly live in damp, shady places?

secenekler.neden: For fertilization, the sperm must swim through water to the egg. Also, a moss has no vascular bundles to carry water.
Mosses carry out photosynthesis, so they need light.
Mosses have no true roots. They hold on with rhizoids.

cards.p: Ferns, horsetails and club mosses have xylem and phloem. They form true roots, stems and leaves. However, these plants have no seeds or flowers. They reproduce with spores.

once.soru: What are the brown dots on the underside of a fern leaf?

secenekler.neden: A fern does not make seeds. Spores form inside these sacs.
A fern has no seeds.
These are the plant's normal reproductive structures.

cards.h: Alternation of generations: gametophyte and sporophyte
cards.p: A 2n cell has two of each chromosome, and an n cell has one. In alternation of generations, the 2n sporophyte makes spores by meiosis. A spore grows into the n gametophyte, and the gametophyte makes gametes.

cards.h: How did the dominant generation change?
cards.p: As you just saw, the gametophyte is dominant in mosses and the sporophyte is dominant in ferns. In seed plants, the gametophyte stays microscopic. Pollen is the male gametophyte, and the embryo sac is the female gametophyte.

cards.p: In seed plants, pollen is carried by wind or animals, so fertilization does not depend on water. A seed is made of an embryo, stored food and a coat. It can wait through drought and sprouts when conditions are right.

cards.key: A spore is a single cell. A seed is a multicellular structure made of an embryo, stored food and a coat.

once.soru: What advantage does a seed have over a spore?

secenekler.neden: A seed holds an embryo, a store of food to nourish it and a protective coat. A spore is a single cell.
A spore is a single cell, so it is much lighter than a seed.
A spore forms by meiosis, while a seed develops after fertilization.

cards.p: Pine, spruce, fir and juniper are gymnosperms. Their seeds sit exposed on cone scales. These plants have no flowers or fruits, and their pollen is carried by the wind. Most stay green all year.

cards.p: In angiosperms, the ovule is protected inside the ovary, and the ovary becomes the fruit. Double fertilization happens only in this group. One sperm forms the zygote, and the other forms the endosperm, the food tissue in the seed.

once.soru: Which part of the flower does a cherry fruit develop from?

secenekler.neden: After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovule inside it becomes the seed.
The petals fall off after fertilization.
Pollen is the male gametophyte, and it does not become a fruit.

cards.h: Monocots and dicots: stems and leaves
cards.p: Angiosperms are divided by their number of cotyledons, or seed leaves. In monocots, leaf veins are parallel and vascular bundles are scattered. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a cambium.

once.soru: A plant has leaves with parallel veins. Which group is it in?

secenekler.neden: Parallel veins are a sign of monocots. Wheat, corn and tulips are examples.
In dicots, the veins form a network.
The cotyledon split is used only for angiosperms.

cards.h: Monocots and dicots: roots and flowers
cards.p: Monocots have fibrous roots, and their flower parts come in multiples of 3. Wheat and tulips are examples. Dicots have a taproot, and their flower parts come in multiples of 4 or 5. Beans and roses are examples. To identify a plant, look at several features together.

cards.p: Plants are the producers on land. They release oxygen and take up CO2. Their roots prevent erosion. They give people food, timber, fiber and medicine. Coal also formed from ancient plant forests.

once.soru: When the trees on a slope are cut down, which problem gets worse?

secenekler.neden: Roots hold the soil. When the trees are cut down, rain washes the soil away.
Plant cover does not affect earthquakes.
Other gases cause the thinning of the ozone layer.

cards.p:
• Plants are eukaryotic, multicellular, have cellulose walls and protect an embryo.
• Mosses are nonvascular and seedless. Ferns are vascular, but seedless.
• The gametophyte is dominant in mosses, and the sporophyte in all other plants.
• In gymnosperms the seed is exposed, and in angiosperms it is inside a fruit.
• Monocots have parallel veins and fibrous roots.

quiz.q: Put the life cycle of a fern in order, starting with the sporophyte.
ogeler: The sporophyte (2n) makes spores (n) by meiosis
The spore grows by mitosis and forms the gametophyte (prothallus)
The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis
The gametes fuse and form a zygote (2n)
The zygote grows and forms a new sporophyte
quiz.e: The sporophyte makes haploid spores by meiosis, and a spore grows by mitosis into the gametophyte. The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis. The diploid zygote formed by fertilization grows into a sporophyte again.

quiz.q: Sort each feature into monocot or dicot.
quiz.e: In monocots, veins are parallel, bundles are scattered, roots are fibrous and flower parts come in multiples of 3. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a taproot. Their embryos have two cotyledons.

quiz.q: The cells of a moss's green, leafy plant have 10 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in the cells of this moss's sporophyte?
quiz.e: The green plant we see in a moss is the gametophyte, and n = 10. The sporophyte grows from the zygote formed when two gametes fuse. That is why it has 2n = 20 chromosomes.

quiz.q: What is the main feature that sets a pine apart from an apple tree?
o: The apple's seed is inside a fruit, and the pine's is exposed.
The pine reproduces by spores, and the apple by seeds.
The apple has vascular bundles, and the pine does not.
The pine does not photosynthesize, and the apple does.
quiz.e: Both are vascular seed plants. The difference lies in how the seed is protected. A pine is a gymnosperm and has no flowers or fruit. An apple tree is an angiosperm.
y: A pine also reproduces by seeds. The difference is whether the seed is inside a fruit or exposed.
A pine is also a vascular plant. The main difference is whether the seed is enclosed in a fruit.
A pine has green leaves and carries out photosynthesis. The difference is whether the seed is exposed or enclosed.
